Re:        PJM Interconnection L.L.C., Docket Nos. EL25-49-000 and -001
           Supplemental Informational Report

Dear Secretary Reese:

           As referenced in the January 20, 2026 informational report, 1 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.

(“PJM”) submits this supplemental informational filing with additional detail regarding the

timeline and process for developing the revisions to the backstop procurement tariff construct and

the timing of commencing the revised backstop procurement process to the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“Commission”).

      I.       INFORMATIONAL FILING

           PJM and stakeholders have commenced the process for developing the reliability backstop

procurement construct at the February 6, 2026 Reliability Backstop Procurement Workshop.2

Under the current timeline, PJM is targeting implementation of a reliability backstop procurement

prior to the December 2026 Base Residual Auction for the 2029/2030 Delivery Year, with a

specific target (subject to potential revision) of running such an auction in September 2026. 3

        Consistent with the above targets, PJM would plan to make a filing to meet the above

planned auction timeline. In order to provide for stakeholder input while balancing the need for

timely presentation of a proposed auction design to the Commission, PJM is planning several

workshops through mid-March. 4 PJM and stakeholders are therefore already actively in the

process of developing the forthcoming revised backstop procurement process, as evidenced by the

several proposals already submitted for consideration. 5 Specifically, at the February 17, 2026

workshop, stakeholders presented various initial proposals, and, on the next day, PJM discussed

its initial thoughts and design of a reliability backstop construct with stakeholders. Additionally,

stakeholder meetings on the reliability backstop process are currently scheduled for February 24,

2026, February 25, 2026, March 4, 2026, and March 5, 2026. Additional meetings to discuss the

reliability backstop construct will be scheduled as needed with the goal of ultimately implementing

         II.     CONCLUSION

         PJM pledges to keep the Commission informed of the timeline for submission of a filing

to the Commission if changes to the current timeline become necessary. PJM appreciates the

Commission and stakeholders’ dedication and understanding given the tight timelines and tasks

ahead.
